facts.statement: Sidney Haughton originally named the species Plateosaurus cullingworthi in 1924 based on a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: Sidney Haughton named Plateosaurus cullingworthi in 1924 from a partial skeleton, type specimen SAM 3341, 3345, 3347, 3350–51, 3603, 3607.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene reassessed the specimen in 1932 and placed it in the new genus Plateosauravus.
facts.quote: Friedrich von Huene reassessed it in 1932 as belonging to a new genus, which he named Plateosauravus.

facts.statement: More than a dozen additional partial skeletons were discovered in Kruger National Park by game warden Adriaan Louw on March 27, 1995.
facts.quote: More than a dozen additional partial skeletons have been found in the Kruger National Park after a discovery by game warden Adriaan Louw on 27 March 1995.

facts.statement: Plateosauravus belongs to the parent group Plateosauridae.
Plateosauravus is classified within the class Saurischia.
The time range for Plateosauravus is from the Norian to the Rhaetian, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Plateosauravus should be classified as Euskelosaurus, which some researchers consider a nomen dubium based on undiagnostic material.
facts.quote: Jacques van Heerden reassigned it to Euskelosaurus in 1979, and this has been how it was usually considered. However, recent study indicates that Euskelosaurus is based on undiagnostic material and thus a nomen dubium; in his series of sauropodomorph and basal sauropod papers, Adam Yates has recommended no longer using Euskelosaurus and has suggested the use of Plateosauravus instead.

rejected.statement: Plateosauravus lived during the Late Triassic in the Elliot Formation of South Africa.
rejected.quote: Plateosauravus ('grandfather of Plateosaurus') is a basal plateosaurian of uncertain affinities from the Late Triassic Elliot Formation of South Africa.
